title: Estimated lumbar passive tissue moment at L5/S1 vs lumbar flexion during standing trunk bending at three speeds (EMG-assisted model)
condition: standing forward bending, knees straight; passive moment = external - EMG-assisted active moment (MODEL-DERIVED)

quantity.name: lumbar passive tissue moment (lumped, incl. passive muscle)
quantity.definition: difference between the total external moment about L5/S1 (multi-segment dynamic model from motion tracking and anthropometry) and the active muscle moment from an EMG-assisted model (Marras & Granata 1997 type), averaged within 5-deg lumbar-flexion intervals from upright; lumbar angle = T12-L5 motion-sensor difference

source.sample: 12 healthy young males (student population), no back or lower-extremity injury

protocol.summary: Upright to full trunk flexion with straight knees in 3, 5 or 7 s (paced), 4 replications each, randomised; EMG of trunk muscles normalised to MVC; Motion Star sensors (T12, L5 etc.). ARB = point where the active moment peaks.
how_to_simulate: Standing posture, pelvis free to rotate (hip flexion) as in natural toe-touch bending; impose the trunk flexion kinematics with lumbar flexion (T12-L5) increasing from upright to ~45 deg
Compute the passive moment about L5/S1 with zero muscle activation (passive tissues + passive muscle), at quasi-static speed
Average the passive moment within each 5-deg lumbar-flexion interval from upright and compare with the slow (7 s) series; speed had no significant effect
protocol.notes: MODEL-DERIVED: the 'measured' passive moment depends on the EMG-assisted model's active moment; use with lower weight than direct passive (frictionless-table) tests. Total passive moment at full flexion ~120 Nm (text). Fit parameters of Eq. 1 (sigma, beta) not extracted because the equation is garbled in the source text.
